extracted.intended_audience: federal agency officials, regulators, administrative practitioners, policymakers, and counsel involved in rulemaking, adjudication, and administrative process design
extracted.subtask_description: An index of Administrative Conference of the United States (ACUS) recommendations—topic-specific guidance and best practices intended to improve federal administrative procedure across rulemaking, adjudication, public engagement, and related processes. The page summarizes adopted recommendations and statements and links to full texts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation development and adoption process
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendations are developed by committees of ACUS members, typically with the support of expert consultants and ACUS staff, and are adopted by the full membership at twice-yearly plenary sessions. Adopted recommendations are published on the ACUS website and in the Federal Register. The Chair and ACUS staff undertake activities to encourage federal agencies to carry out recommendations adopted by ACUS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACUS sometimes adopts “Statements,” which express the agency's views on a particular matter without making a formal recommendation. Statements are developed through the same process as recommendations but typically set forth issues, conclusions from a study, or comments, rather than recommendations. ACUS has adopted 20 statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proactive Disclosure of Agency Legal Materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies produce many kinds of legal materials, including documents that establish, interpret, apply, explain, or address the enforcement of legal rights and obligations, along with constraints imposed, implemented, or enforced by or upon an agency. Many principal statutes govern the public disclosure of these materials; however, there are inconsistencies and…
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This Recommendation (2023-1) addresses inconsistencies in public disclosure of agency legal materials and provides guidance for when and how agencies should proactively disclose such materials. (Link to full text for detailed standards.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Virtual Public Engagement in Agency Rulemaking
rubrics_metrics.description: In recent years, and especially during the COVID-19 pandemic, agencies increasingly have used widely available, internet-based videoconferencing software to engage with the public during rulemakings. Virtual public engagement can help broaden participation in agency rulemakings by reducing barriers that people—especially members of historically underserved communities—face.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation (2023-2) offers best practices for designing and conducting virtual public engagement to broaden participation and reduce barriers; consult full text for specifics on accessibility, outreach, and procedural safeguards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using Algorithmic Tools in Retrospective Review of Agency Rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Retrospective review is the process by which agencies assess existing rules and decide whether they need to be revisited. Agencies may be able to leverage algorithmic tools, including artificial intelligence, to more efficiently, cost-effectively, and accurately identify rules that are outmoded or redundant, contain typographic errors or inaccurate cross-references, or might…
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation (2023-3) describes how algorithmic tools can assist retrospective review and addresses benefits and limitations; see full recommendation for guidance on tool selection, validation, and oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Online Processes in Agency Adjudication
rubrics_metrics.description: To improve the accuracy, efficiency, and accessibility of their adjudications, agencies have deployed online processes by which parties, representatives, and others can perform common tasks such as filing, serving, and viewing forms, briefs, evidence, and other case records or materials. These processes range from simple email-based systems to robust online self-…
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation (2023-4) provides standards and best practices for deploying online adjudication processes, balancing efficiency with due process, privacy, and access concerns; consult full text for implementation guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Practices for Adjudication Not Involving an Evidentiary Hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: In many federal administrative adjudications, parties have no right to an evidentiary hearing. Such adjudications include many decisions regarding grants, licenses, or permits; immigration and naturalization; national security; the regulation of banks; land-use requests; and a wide variety of other matters. As diverse as these adjudications are, they do share some…
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation (2023-5) identifies shared issues and recommends best practices for fair and effective non-evidentiary adjudications; see full recommendation for specific procedural safeguards and process design elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identifying and Reducing Burdens on the Public in Administrative Proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Each year, millions of people navigate administrative processes to access benefits and services and otherwise obtain assistance for themselves and their families. The public spends significant time and effort learning about these programs and complying with their requirements, and efforts to comply can result in stress, stigma, or other psychological harms. These learning…
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation (2023-6) focuses on identifying and reducing procedural burdens, cognitive load, and stigma in administrative processes; full text contains concrete measures agencies can take to simplify procedures and reduce harm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improving Timeliness in Agency Adjudication
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal agencies adjudicate millions of cases each year and members of the public depend on the timely adjudication of those cases. Delayed adjudication, especially given the possible added time of judicial review, can have significant consequences, particularly for members of historically underserved communities. Building on earlier ACUS recommendations, this Recommendation…
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation (2023-7) provides guidance to improve timeliness, including process redesign, resource allocation, and metrics for monitoring delay; see the full recommendation for implementation approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: User Fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal agencies charge user fees as part of many programs to, for example, shift the costs of a program from taxpayers to those persons or entities whom the program directly benefits, supplement general revenue, or incentivize or discourage certain behavior. User fee programs vary significantly in their design. When designing user fee programs, Congress and agencies…
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation (2023-8) offers principles for designing and administering user fee programs, addressing objectives, equity, legal constraints, and implementation; consult full text for detailed criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contractors in Rulemaking
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies rely on private contractors to perform many kinds of services in support of their rulemaking activities. These services can occur at any stage of the rulemaking process. They also vary in levels of complexity, ranging from relatively simple tasks such as sorting public comments to more complex matters such as preparing regulatory impact analyses or…
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation (2022-1) discusses appropriate roles, oversight, and transparency for contractors in rulemaking; full recommendation describes safeguards to preserve integrity and public trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improving Notice of Regulatory Changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Each year federal agencies issue hundreds of thousands of pages of legislative rules, guidance documents, adjudicative orders, notices, and other materials that affect administrative programs. Although the law generally requires these materials be made public, individuals and organizations may lack the resources or expertise to track and understand regulatory changes that…
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation (2022-2) provides approaches to improve notice, discoverability, and public understanding of regulatory changes; see the full text for specific notification, indexing, and outreach recommendations.
